title: Binder5 to GPX4 degrader | pre-2026 evidence
objective: Accelerate removal of endogenous GPX4 protein while retaining binder engagement; distinguish direct turnover from inhibition, suppressed synthesis, insolubility and secondary ferroptotic loss.
coordinate_note: All construct coordinates are 1-based inclusive. binder5 identity is provisional: prior user-supplied sequence, 61 encoded residues. Human GPX4 P36969 is the target, not the binder accession. Literature cutoff: publication before 2026-01-01. Cell model not specified; assume mammalian intracellular expression targeting an accessible cytosolic pool. Native sequence database retrieved 2026-11-16, distinct from literature cutoff.

hypotheses.question: Can a compact RRRG tail drive GPX4 turnover in trans?
hypotheses.mechanism: A binder-linked terminal degron recruits endogenous UPS machinery while binder5 engages GPX4.
hypotheses.measurement: D02 versus D03 and D01: GPX4 pulse-chase half-life and total abundance, at overlapping measured binder exposure and preserved engagement. Common assay: early denaturing GPX4 abundance, pulse–chase of existing GPX4, binder abundance/turnover, GPX4 transcript, soluble/insoluble recovery and activity; parallel ferroptosis protection separates downstream damage. Proteasome/lysosome perturbations require inhibitor-only controls. Assign GPX4 ubiquitin under denaturing isolation.

hypotheses.question: Can a defined KLHDC2-recognition tail drive GPX4 turnover?
hypotheses.mechanism: Exposed SPPPMAGG recruits endogenous CRL2–KLHDC2 to a GPX4-bound binder.
hypotheses.measurement: D04 versus D05 and D01; require loss of effect after KLHDC2 depletion and restoration by WT complementation, alongside direct GPX4 turnover. Common assay: early denaturing GPX4 abundance, pulse–chase of existing GPX4, binder abundance/turnover, GPX4 transcript, soluble/insoluble recovery and activity; parallel ferroptosis protection separates downstream damage. Proteasome/lysosome perturbations require inhibitor-only controls. Assign GPX4 ubiquitin under denaturing isolation.

hypotheses.question: Does binder self-ubiquitination limit the RRRG fusion?
hypotheses.mechanism: Replacing the eight binder lysines with arginine may reduce competing ubiquitin attachment to the binder.
hypotheses.measurement: Full factorial contrast D02–D03 versus D06–D07, with binder turnover, affinity and intracellular exposure measured separately. Common assay: early denaturing GPX4 abundance, pulse–chase of existing GPX4, binder abundance/turnover, GPX4 transcript, soluble/insoluble recovery and activity; parallel ferroptosis protection separates downstream damage. Proteasome/lysosome perturbations require inhibitor-only controls. Assign GPX4 ubiquitin under denaturing isolation.

hypotheses.question: Does a tethered E3 module produce GPX4 turnover when compact tails do not?
hypotheses.mechanism: Binder5 replaces CHIP’s native TPR recognition module while CHIPΔTPR retains dimerization and E2-dependent ubiquitination.
hypotheses.measurement: D08 versus E2-impaired D09, guideless D10 and D01: denaturing GPX4 ubiquitination, shortened half-life and proteasome dependence; check unrelated proteins and viable-cell recovery. Common assay: early denaturing GPX4 abundance, pulse–chase of existing GPX4, binder abundance/turnover, GPX4 transcript, soluble/insoluble recovery and activity; parallel ferroptosis protection separates downstream damage. Proteasome/lysosome perturbations require inhibitor-only controls. Assign GPX4 ubiquitin under denaturing isolation.

method.homolog_source: UniRef50_Q9Y6D0; 159 retrieved UniProt entries; 2026-11-16. U converted to C only in alignment inputs; native graft contains no U.
method.comparison_set: UniProtKB members of UniRef50_Q9Y6D0, the UniRef50 cluster containing Q9Y6D0: the same protein in other species, clustered by UniProt at 50% identity with an 80% length-overlap requirement. ORTHOLOG level: scores answer what this protein needs.
method.alignment: multiple alignment by FAMSA via pyfamsa 0.7.0, projected onto reference coordinates by dropping columns where the reference is gapped. It can score positions that MAFFT leaves unscored, with weak support, so read per-position coverage alongside the score
method.weighting: Henikoff position-based sequence weights, computed over variable columns only
method.effective_sequences_definition: Neff = sum(1/n_i), n_i counting sequences at least 80% identical to sequence i over positions where both have a residue (itself included); pairs overlapping less than 50% of the reference are not counted as similar. Reported unnormalised and divided by reference length; normalisation is not standardised in the literature, so compare only against values computed the same way. This is NOT the sum of the Henikoff weights, which is rescaled to the sequence count by construction and therefore always equals it.
method.score: Jensen-Shannon divergence against Robinson & Robinson background, scaled by column occupancy (Capra & Singh 2007)
method.normalization: U-to-C in alignment/scoring inputs only; donor retains native U. Grafted residues 84–91 contain no U.

precedent_search.scope: Separate target/mechanism and 2024–2025 primary-work searches returned before selecting candidates: GPX4+BindCraft+binder5, GPX4 PROTAC/CMA, RRRG/K-to-R, KLHDC2 peptide AdPROM, CHIP bioPROTAC, E2 geometry, delivery-dependent failure. Followed cited and citing studies from 2014/2023/2024 into 2025. All design-supporting literature published before 2026-01-01; later publications excluded, including studies accepted in 2025 but first published in 2026. No eligible binder5-specific structure or validation was established.
precedent_search.reason: Design consequence: retain intact binder, keep C-end motifs terminal, compare small recruiters with direct E3 fusion, include binder turnover and target-initiation limits; do not infer efficacy from affinity alone.
